recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It restores the applied FHIR-I decision without broadening scope and preserves later metadata cleanups already made to the CodeSystem, ValueSet, and profile.
issue_request: FHIR-46086 was Applied as Persuasive with Modification for R6. It requested a ValueSet for the FHIRPath Patch operation type codes and the final resolution required a CodeSystem, ValueSet, and core Parameters profile for validating FHIRPath Patch Parameters instances.
initial_application: Commit 3f6c131b0b12db47ebcc0e069f9ea64666d82f74 added the patch-operation CodeSystem and ValueSet XML files, the fhirpath-patch Parameters profile, an ImplementationGuide reference for the profile, a fhirpatch.html profile link, and active source/fhir.ini registrations for the CodeSystem and ValueSet.
additional_context: The current source still contained the terminology files and profile, and the profile required http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/patch-operation for the operation type code. A later unrelated FHIR-48664 commit, 2f3664baf35835a0d3cac9be76a13175c52bc9a1, commented out only the fhir.ini CodeSystem and ValueSet registrations. FHIR-48393 comments confirmed FHIRPath Patch should stay in core because it supports the Patch operation.
reconciliation: Uncommented the patch-operation entries in source/fhir.ini under [codesystems] and [valuesets], restoring parameters/codesystem-patch-operation.xml and parameters/valueset-patch-operation.xml to current build scope. No terminology content or profile changes were needed.

related_jiras.note: Its implementation commit unintentionally commented out the FHIRPath Patch terminology registrations while addressing an unrelated ElementDefinition binding rule.
Later comments state that FHIRPath Patch should remain in core because it is a Parameters profile used by the Patch operation.
Earlier published clarification for the FHIRPath Patch page established the current page context but did not decide the terminology ValueSet request.
